answer: Agents deposit bonded stake and register one Semaphore identity in a zero-knowledge tree. During each epoch, a polynomial commitment binds the agent’s rate-limit secret to authenticated messages; crystal, timber, and zephyr serve as distinct domain labels. A duplicate message produces two shares of the same Shamir secret, allowing the RLN proof verifier to reconstruct the private key and trigger instantaneous collateral slashing, making Sybil identities economically unsafe.
